hotspots.title: July 2007
hotspots.body: The fifth film opened in July 2007, the first of four directed by David Yates, who would guide the series to its end.

hotspots.title: A hall made of light
hotspots.body: The towering shelves of glass spheres were realised largely as digital effects; their sheer number, and the way they shatter in the chase, made physical props impractical.

hotspots.title: The longest book, a lean film
hotspots.body: Its source is the longest book of the seven, yet at about 138 minutes the film is one of the shortest in the series, built around a few strong set pieces.

hotspots.title: A smile to fear
hotspots.body: Imelda Staunton played the new Defence teacher, a figure of pink cardigans, kitten plates and absolute control. The performance made her one of the series' most memorable villains.

hotspots.title: Found in an open call
hotspots.body: Evanna Lynch won the role of the dreamy Luna Lovegood through an open audition that drew thousands of hopefuls.

hotspots.title: A Ministry underground
hotspots.body: The vast Ministry atrium was built as a set at the studio, its tiled, panelled look drawing on the older stations of the London Underground.

hotspots.title: A new voice
hotspots.body: Nicholas Hooper composed the score, adding urgent percussion for the secret lessons and a wistful theme for the school year.

hotspots.title: A secret classroom
hotspots.body: Students teach each other to defend themselves in a room that appears only when needed. The film plays it as joyful rebellion before the danger arrives.

hotspots.title: A name on the shelf
hotspots.body: Deep among the rows, one small sphere carries Harry's name. What it holds, and who wants it, drives the film's final act.

hotspots.title: Behind the veil
hotspots.body: The confrontation ends beside a stone archway hung with a drifting veil, the series' quietest image of loss.

hotspots.title: A loud exit
hotspots.body: The twins' fireworks farewell to the tyrannical teacher was staged as a burst of digital colour that briefly fills the school with light.
